facts.text: Greater Montréal's aerospace sector has more than 43,000 highly skilled jobs, equivalent to one worker in fifty in the region, with five prime contractors and 219 suppliers.
Montréal accounts for almost 49% of Canada's aerospace workforce, 57% of sales and 70% of R&D, and 80% of Québec aerospace production is exported.
Approximately 11 million international and domestic tourists visited Montréal in 2024, up 7.8% from the previous year, and spent over $6.01 billion during their trips.
In 2024, 539 business events were held in Montréal, bringing 960,000 delegates and visitors and $395 million in economic spinoffs.

overview: Montreal is Canada's second-largest city, with about 1.8 million residents in the 2021 Census, up 3.4% from 1.7 million in 2016. Its 816,338 occupied dwellings sit on just 364.74 square kilometres, making it one of the densest markets in the country, and the median age is 39.6.

Aerospace, tourism and business events drive the economy, and the customer base is largely French-speaking. A local business competes in a crowded, bilingual market where visibility in French matters as much as price.
